name: Gaya Tumuli
description: Across southern South Korea, seven clusters of grassy burial mounds mark where the Gaya people buried their rulers between the 1st and 6th centuries CE. The mounds often crown ridgelines, with the grandest tombs at the highest points. Together they show a confederacy of independent, equal city-states that shared a culture but never merged into one kingdom, a rarity in early Korea.
